title: City of King City Charter Modernization Amendment
ballot_label: Caption: City of King City Charter Modernization Amendment. Question: Shall the City of King City amend and restate the existing Charter to modernize, update, and clarify Charter provisions?
summary: King City asks voters to amend and restate its 2006 city charter. The measure adds definitions, mirrors the League of Oregon Cities model charter, clarifies vacancies and councilor duties and prohibitions, removes the prohibition on councilor compensation, adds a charter review section, and moves duties of the City Manager, Judge and City Attorney to ordinance or resolution. It keeps the council-manager form and the current way of selecting the mayor.
yes_means: A yes vote amends and restates the King City charter as described in the ballot title.
no_means: A no vote leaves the current King City charter in effect.
fiscal_impact: The ballot title and explanatory statement give no cost or revenue estimate. The measure would remove the charter's prohibition on compensation for councilors.

arguments.author: Vincent Arditi
arguments.statement: Vincent Arditi argues the amendment does not change the present system in which the city council chooses the mayor, and urges a no vote so residents can vote for their mayor.
arguments.excerpt: 4 out of 7 council members still control their choice for your mayor as selected by city council.
